claim: SAMap identifies homologous cell types with shared expression programs across distant species within phyla.
source: This new method, SAMap, identifies homologous cell types with shared expression programs across distant species within phyla, even in complex examples where homologous tissues emerge from distinct germ layers.
evidence: The abstract states this as a primary finding of the study, and the manuscript provides multiple examples including zebrafish-frog and planarian-schistosome comparisons.

claim: SAMap identifies homologous cell types even in complex examples where homologous tissues emerge from distinct germ layers.
source: This new method, SAMap, identifies homologous cell types with shared expression programs across distant species within phyla, even in complex examples where homologous tissues emerge from distinct germ layers.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this capability, and Figure 2B shows secretory cell types mapping across germ layers.

claim: SAMap finds many genes with more similar expression to their paralogs than their orthologs.
source: SAMap also finds many genes with more similar expression to their paralogs than their orthologs, suggesting paralog substitution may be more common in evolution than previously appreciated.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, and Figure 3 provides data showing 565 genes with markedly higher expression correlations with paralogs than orthologs.

claim: Paralog substitution may be more common in evolution than previously appreciated.
source: SAMap also finds many genes with more similar expression to their paralogs than their orthologs, suggesting paralog substitution may be more common in evolution than previously appreciated.
evidence: This is presented as an interpretation of the data on paralog expression correlations.

claim: Comparing species across animal phyla, spanning sponge to mouse, reveals ancient contractile and stem cell families.
source: Lastly, comparing species across animal phyla, spanning sponge to mouse, reveals ancient contractile and stem cell families, which may have arisen early in animal evolution.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, and Figure 5C shows network graphs of highly connected contractile and neural cell type families across all seven species.

claim: Ancient contractile and stem cell families may have arisen early in animal evolution.
source: Lastly, comparing species across animal phyla, spanning sponge to mouse, reveals ancient contractile and stem cell families, which may have arisen early in animal evolution.
evidence: This is presented as an interpretation of the cross-phyla cell type family data.

claim: Recent comparative single-cell analyses are mostly limited to species within the same phylum.
source: However, recent comparative single-cell analyses are mostly limited to species within the same phylum (Baron et al., 2016; Geirsdottir et al., 2019; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2018; Tosches et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous comparative studies.

claim: Comparisons across longer evolutionary distances and across phyla are challenging due to diversification of gene regulatory programs during evolution.
source: Comparisons across longer evolutionary distances and across phyla are challenging for two major reasons. First, gene regulatory programs diversify during evolution, diminishing the similarities in cell-type-specific gene expression patterns.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about evolutionary processes.

claim: Complex gene evolutionary history causes distantly related organisms to share few one-to-one gene orthologs.
source: Second, complex gene evolutionary history causes distantly related organisms to share few one-to-one gene orthologs (Nehrt et al., 2011), which are often relied upon for comparative studies (Briggs et al., 2018; Shafer, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies on gene orthology.

claim: Paralogs may be more functionally similar than orthologs across species due to differential gain, loss, or partitioning events among paralogs.
source: This effect is compounded by the growing evidence suggesting that paralogs may be more functionally similar than orthologs across species, due to differential gain (neo-functionalization), loss (non-functionalization), or partitioning (sub-functionalization) events among paralogs (Nehrt et al., 2011; Prince and Pickett, 2002; Stamboulian et al., 2020; Studer and Robinson-Rechavi, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous studies on paralog function.

claim: SAMap relaxes the constraints imposed by sequence orthology by using expression similarity between mapped cells to infer the relative contributions of homologous genes.
source: SAMap relaxes the constraints imposed by sequence orthology, using expression similarity between mapped cells to infer the relative contributions of homologous genes, which in turn refines the cell type mapping.
evidence: This describes a key methodological feature of SAMap as implemented in the algorithm.

claim: SAMap uses a graph-based data integration technique to identify reciprocally connected cell types across species with greater robustness than previous single-cell data integration methods.
source: In addition, SAMap uses a graph-based data integration technique to identify reciprocally connected cell types across species with greater robustness than previous single-cell data integration methods (Haghverdi et al., 2018; Hie et al., 2019; Polański et al., 2019; Stuart et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by benchmarking comparisons shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Seven whole-body cell atlases from species spanning animal phylogeny were compared using SAMap.
source: Using SAMap, we compared seven whole-body cell atlases from species spanning animal phylogeny, which have divergent transcriptomes and complex molecular homologies (Figure 1A–B and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Figure 1A shows the phylogenetic relationships among the seven species analyzed.

claim: SAMap found broad concordance between transcriptomic signatures and ontogenetic relationships in developing frog and zebrafish embryos.
source: We found broad concordance between transcriptomic signatures and ontogenetic relationships, which validated our mapping results, yet also detected striking examples of homologous cell types emerging from different germ layers.
evidence: Figure 2B shows that SAMap linked 26 out of 27 expected pairs based on previous annotations.

claim: SAMap detected striking examples of homologous cell types emerging from different germ layers in frog and zebrafish.
source: We found broad concordance between transcriptomic signatures and ontogenetic relationships, which validated our mapping results, yet also detected striking examples of homologous cell types emerging from different germ layers.
evidence: Figure 2B highlights secretory cell types that map across germ layers.

claim: SAMap found one-to-one homologies even between cell subtypes when comparing a planarian flatworm and a parasitic blood fluke.
source: We next extended the comparison to animals from the same phylum but with highly divergent body plans, using a planarian flatworm and a parasitic blood fluke, and found one-to-one homologies even between cell subtypes.
evidence: Figure 4 shows detailed mappings between planarian and schistosome cell types including stem cell subpopulations.

claim: SAMap identified densely interconnected cell type families broadly shared across animals, including contractile and stem cells.
source: Comparing all seven species from sponge to mouse, we identified densely interconnected cell type families broadly shared across animals, including contractile and stem cells, along with their respective gene expression programs.
evidence: Figure 5C shows network graphs of highly connected cell type families including contractile and stem cells.

claim: Homologous cell types often exhibit differential expression of orthologs and similar expression of paralogs.
source: Lastly, we noticed that homologous cell types often exhibit differential expression of orthologs and similar expression of paralogs, suggesting that the substitution and swapping of paralogs in cell types may be more common in evolution than previously appreciated.
evidence: Figure 3 shows examples of paralog substitutions and quantifies their prevalence.

claim: The substitution and swapping of paralogs in cell types may be more common in evolution than previously appreciated.
source: Lastly, we noticed that homologous cell types often exhibit differential expression of orthologs and similar expression of paralogs, suggesting that the substitution and swapping of paralogs in cell types may be more common in evolution than previously appreciated.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the paralog substitution data presented in Figure 3.

claim: SAMap iterates between two modules: constructing a gene-gene bipartite graph and projecting datasets into a joint manifold representation.
source: SAMap iterates between two modules. The first module constructs a gene-gene bipartite graph with cross-species edges connecting homologous gene pairs, initially weighted by protein sequence similarity (Figure 1C). In the second module, SAMap uses the gene-gene graph to project the two single-cell transcriptomic datasets into a joint, lower-dimensional manifold representation, from which each cell's mutual cross-species neighbors are linked to stitch the cell atlases together (Figure 1D).
evidence: Figure 1C shows the SAMap workflow with these two modules.

claim: SAMap initially weights cross-species edges in the gene-gene bipartite graph by protein sequence similarity.
source: The first module constructs a gene-gene bipartite graph with cross-species edges connecting homologous gene pairs, initially weighted by protein sequence similarity (Figure 1C).
evidence: This describes the initial step of the SAMap algorithm.

claim: SAMap uses expression correlations between homologous genes to reweight edges in the gene-gene homology graph.
source: Then, using the joint manifold, the expression correlations between homologous genes are computed and used to reweight the edges in the gene-gene homology graph in order to relax SAMap's initial dependence on sequence similarity.
evidence: This describes the iterative refinement step of the SAMap algorithm.

claim: SAMap continues iterating until convergence, defined as when the cross-species mapping does not significantly change between iterations.
source: The new homology graph is used as input to the subsequent iteration of SAMap, and the algorithm continues until convergence, defined as when the cross-species mapping does not significantly change between iterations (Figure 1E).
evidence: Figure 1E shows the convergence of SAMap evaluated by RMSE of alignment scores.

claim: SAMap produced a combined manifold with a high degree of cross-species alignment while maintaining high resolution for distinguishing cell types in zebrafish and Xenopus.
source: SAMap produced a combined manifold with a high degree of cross-species alignment while maintaining high resolution for distinguishing cell types in each species (Figure 2A).
evidence: Figure 2A shows the UMAP projection of the combined zebrafish and Xenopus manifolds.

claim: SAMap linked 26 out of 27 expected pairs based on previous annotations in the zebrafish-Xenopus comparison.
source: SAMap revealed broad agreement between transcriptomic similarity and developmental ontogeny, linking 26 out of 27 expected pairs based on previous annotations (Figure 2B and Supplementary file 2; Briggs et al., 2018).
evidence: Figure 2B shows the Sankey plot summarizing cell type mappings.

claim: The embryonic kidney (pronephric duct/mesenchyme) was the only exception not linked between zebrafish and Xenopus, potentially indicating that their gene expression programs have significantly diverged.
source: The only exception is the embryonic kidney (pronephric duct/mesenchyme), potentially indicating that their gene expression programs have significantly diverged.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the mapping results and an interpretation of what it might indicate.

claim: SAMap succeeded in drawing parallels between the development of homologous cell types and matched time points along several cell lineages in zebrafish and Xenopus.
source: In addition, SAMap succeeded in drawing parallels between the development of homologous cell types and matched time points along several cell lineages (Figure 2C).
evidence: Figure 2C shows heatmaps of alignment scores between developmental time points for several lineages.

claim: The exact progression of developmental timing can vary between zebrafish and Xenopus, suggesting that SAMap can quantify heterochrony with cell type resolution.
source: While the concordance was consistent across cell types, we noticed that the exact progression of developmental timing can vary, suggesting that SAMap can quantify heterochrony with cell type resolution.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the developmental timing alignment data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Frog cement gland cells map to zebrafish muc5ac+ secretory epidermal cells.
source: Within ectoderm, frog cement gland cells map to zebrafish muc5ac+ secretory epidermal cells, and frog small secretory cells (SSCs) map to zebrafish pvalb8+ mucous cells (Janicke et al., 2010).
evidence: This mapping is shown in Figure 2B and supported by gene expression data in Figure 2D.

claim: Frog small secretory cells (SSCs) map to zebrafish pvalb8+ mucous cells.
source: Within ectoderm, frog cement gland cells map to zebrafish muc5ac+ secretory epidermal cells, and frog small secretory cells (SSCs) map to zebrafish pvalb8+ mucous cells (Janicke et al., 2010).
evidence: This mapping is shown in Figure 2B and supported by gene expression data in Figure 2D.

claim: Frog SSCs also map weakly to zebrafish endodermal cells.
source: Across germ layers, SSCs also map weakly to zebrafish endodermal cells, and frog ectodermal hatching gland maps to zebrafish mesodermal hatching gland.
evidence: This cross-germ layer mapping is shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Frog ectodermal hatching gland maps to zebrafish mesodermal hatching gland.
source: Across germ layers, SSCs also map weakly to zebrafish endodermal cells, and frog ectodermal hatching gland maps to zebrafish mesodermal hatching gland.
evidence: This cross-germ layer mapping is shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Secretory cell types that differ in developmental origin are linked through a large set of genes, including proteins involved in vesicular protein trafficking and several conserved transcription factors such as myb, foxa1, xbp1, and klf17.
source: These cell types are linked through a large set of genes, including proteins involved in vesicular protein trafficking and several conserved transcription factors (TFs) such as myb, foxa1, xbp1, and klf17 (Figure 2D), which all have documented functions in controlling the differentiation of secretory cell types (Bennett et al., 2007; Dubaissi et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2014).
evidence: Figure 2D shows the expression of these genes in the mapped secretory cell types.

claim: myb, foxa1, xbp1, and klf17 all have documented functions in controlling the differentiation of secretory cell types.
source: These cell types are linked through a large set of genes, including proteins involved in vesicular protein trafficking and several conserved transcription factors (TFs) such as myb, foxa1, xbp1, and klf17 (Figure 2D), which all have documented functions in controlling the differentiation of secretory cell types (Bennett et al., 2007; Dubaissi et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies on these transcription factors.

claim: klf17 is expressed in zebrafish and frog hatching glands and plays essential roles in regulating gland cell specification in both species.
source: For example, klf17 is expressed in zebrafish and frog hatching glands, and plays essential roles in regulating gland cell specification in both species (Kurauchi et al., 2010; Suzuki et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies on klf17 function.

claim: The conserved cell type specification programs between developmentally distinct secretory cells support the notion that they may be transcriptionally and evolutionarily related despite having different developmental origins.
source: Together, the conserved cell type specification programs (Erwin and Davidson, 2009) between developmentally distinct secretory cells support the notion that they may be transcriptionally and evolutionarily related despite having different developmental origins (Arendt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the secretory cell mapping data supported by citations to theoretical frameworks.

claim: Several broadly used single-cell data integration methods (Seurat, LIGER, Harmony, Scanorama, and BBKNN) failed to map the zebrafish and frog atlases when using one-to-one vertebrate orthologs as input.
source: We found that they failed to map the two atlases, yielding minimal alignment between them (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1 show the benchmarking comparison results.

claim: SAMap using one-to-one orthologs identified similar, albeit weaker, cell type mappings compared to using the full homology graph.
source: We also compared the results when restricting SAMap to using the one-to-one orthologs instead of the full homology graph. Even when removing the many-to-many gene homologies and the iterative refinement of the homology graph, we identified similar, albeit weaker, cell type mappings.
evidence: This comparison is shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: For the frog and zebrafish comparison, SAMap's performance is owed in large part to its robust, atlas stitching approach.
source: This suggests that, at least for the frog and zebrafish comparison, SAMap's performance is owed in large part to its robust, atlas stitching approach.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the benchmarking results comparing SAMap to other methods.

claim: SAMap is robust to incomplete cell type atlases, as demonstrated by systematic downsampling of frog and zebrafish data.
source: Finally, to test if SAMap is robust to incomplete cell type atlases, we downsampled the frog and zebrafish data by systematically removing individual cell types.
evidence: The results of this downsampling experiment are described in the text and Supplementary file 3.

claim: Cell types whose homologous partners were removed mapped weakly to closely related cell types in the downsampling experiment.
source: We found that cell types whose homologous partners were removed mapped weakly to closely related cell types, some of which were already present in the original mapping.
evidence: This describes the results of the downsampling robustness test.

claim: SAMap is more sensitive in linking homologous cell types compared to other existing methods.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that SAMap is more sensitive in linking homologous cell types compared to other existing methods, exhibits high robustness when applied to incomplete datasets, and yields mapping results that are well supported by conserved gene expression programs.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the benchmarking and robustness testing results.

claim: SAMap exhibits high robustness when applied to incomplete datasets.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that SAMap is more sensitive in linking homologous cell types compared to other existing methods, exhibits high robustness when applied to incomplete datasets, and yields mapping results that are well supported by conserved gene expression programs.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the downsampling robustness testing results.

claim: SAMap yields mapping results that are well supported by conserved gene expression programs.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that SAMap is more sensitive in linking homologous cell types compared to other existing methods, exhibits high robustness when applied to incomplete datasets, and yields mapping results that are well supported by conserved gene expression programs.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the gene expression analysis of mapped cell types.

claim: SAMap selected 8286 vertebrate orthologs and 7093 paralogs for manifold alignment in the zebrafish-Xenopus comparison.
source: In total, SAMap selected 8286 vertebrate orthologs and 7093 paralogs, as enumerated by eggNOG, for manifold alignment.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the SAMap analysis.

claim: 565 genes have markedly higher expression correlations (correlation difference >0.3) with their paralogs than their orthologs in the zebrafish-Xenopus comparison.
source: Among these, 565 genes have markedly higher expression correlations (correlation difference >0.3) with their paralogs than their orthologs (see Figure 3A for examples), and 209 of them have orthologs that are either completely absent or lowly expressed with no cell-type specificity (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Figure 3A shows examples of these paralog substitutions.

claim: 209 genes with paralog substitutions have orthologs that are either completely absent or lowly expressed with no cell-type specificity.
source: Among these, 565 genes have markedly higher expression correlations (correlation difference >0.3) with their paralogs than their orthologs (see Figure 3A for examples), and 209 of them have orthologs that are either completely absent or lowly expressed with no cell-type specificity (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the paralog substitution analysis.

claim: Paralog substitution events are defined as cases where orthologs may have lost or changed their functional roles and were compensated for by their paralogs.
source: We term these events as 'paralog substitutions', as the orthologs may have lost or changed their functional roles at some point and were compensated for by their paralogs.
evidence: This is the definition provided for the term 'paralog substitution' used in the study.

claim: Substituting paralogs were identified in most cell types with some (e.g. dorsal organizer) exhibiting higher rates than others.
source: Substituting paralogs were identified in most cells types with some (e.g. dorsal organizer) exhibiting higher rates than others (Figure 3B), suggesting uneven diversification rates of paralogs across cell types.
evidence: Figure 3B shows paralog substitution scores of all cell types.

claim: Uneven diversification rates of paralogs occur across cell types.
source: Substituting paralogs were identified in most cells types with some (e.g. dorsal organizer) exhibiting higher rates than others (Figure 3B), suggesting uneven diversification rates of paralogs across cell types.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cell type-specific paralog substitution data.

claim: SAMap linked an additional 297 homologous pairs previously unannotated by orthology or paralogy, but which exhibit sequence similarity and high expression correlations (>0.5 Pearson correlation).
source: SAMap also linked an additional 297 homologous pairs previously unannotated by orthology or paralogy, but which exhibit sequence similarity and high expression correlations (>0.5 Pearson correlation).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the SAMap analysis.

claim: The 297 unannotated homologous pairs likely represent unannotated orthologs/paralogs or isofunctional, distantly related homologs.
source: These likely represent unannotated orthologs/paralogs or isofunctional, distantly related homologs (Gabaldón and Koonin, 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the unannotated homologous pairs supported by a citation.

claim: More recent paralogs substitute orthologs at higher rates than more ancient paralogs.
source: We categorized paralogs by the taxonomic level of their most recent shared orthology group and found that more recent paralogs substitute orthologs at higher rates than more ancient paralogs (Figure 3C).
evidence: Figure 3C shows the percentage of paralogs from each phylogenetic age that were substituted.

claim: The observation that more recent paralogs substitute orthologs at higher rates is consistent with the expectation that less diverged genes may be more capable of functionally compensating for each other.
source: This observation is consistent with the expectation that less diverged genes may be more capable of functionally compensating for each other.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the paralog age-dependent substitution rate data.

claim: 70% of paralog substitutions were identified when using only one-to-one orthologs as input for SAMap.
source: To rule out the possibility that these paralogs were linked spuriously during the homology refinement steps of SAMap, we repeated the paralog substitution analysis on an aligned manifold constructed using only one-to-one orthologs. We identified 70% of the paralog substitutions and observed similar patterns in evolutionary time and cell type dependencies (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1 shows the comparison of substitution rates between the original and one-to-one ortholog based analyses.

claim: The other 30% of substitutions not detected when using one-to-one orthologs had smaller correlation differences on the border of the detection threshold.
source: The other 30% of substitutions had smaller correlation differences on the border of our detection threshold (i.e. correlation difference >0.3) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Figure 3—figure supplement 1C shows the distribution of correlation differences for different paralog substitution sets.

claim: Failure to detect 30% of substitutions when using one-to-one orthologs was due to inaccurate imputation of gene expressions across species.
source: Failure to detect these substitutions was due to inaccurate imputation of gene expressions across species when restricting the mapping to one-to-one orthologs, which resulted in weaker alignment with fewer cross-species edges.
evidence: This is an interpretation of why some substitutions were not detected in the one-to-one ortholog analysis.

claim: SAMap has potential in leveraging single-cell gene expression data for pruning networks of homologous genes to identify evolutionary substitution of paralogs.
source: Altogether, these results illustrate the potential of SAMap in leveraging single-cell gene expression data for pruning the networks of homologous genes to identify evolutionary substitution of paralogs and, more generally, identify non-orthologous gene pairs that may perform similar functions in the cell types within which they are expressed.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about SAMap's capabilities based on the paralog substitution analysis.

claim: Planarians live in freshwater and are known for their ability to regenerate.
source: While planarians live in freshwater and are known for their ability to regenerate (Reddien, 2018), schistosomes live as parasites in humans.
evidence: This is established knowledge about planarian biology supported by a citation.

claim: Schistosomes live as parasites in humans.
source: While planarians live in freshwater and are known for their ability to regenerate (Reddien, 2018), schistosomes live as parasites in humans.
evidence: This is established knowledge about schistosome biology.

claim: SAMap revealed broad cell type homology between schistosomes and planarians.
source: SAMap revealed broad cell type homology between schistosomes and planarians.
evidence: Figure 4A shows the combined manifolds with mapped cell types.

claim: The schistosome had cells mapped to planarian neoblasts, as well as most differentiated tissues including neural, muscle, intestine, epidermis, parenchymal, protonephridia, and cathepsin+ cells.
source: The schistosome had cells mapped to the planarian stem cells, called neoblasts, as well as most of the differentiated tissues: neural, muscle, intestine, epidermis, parenchymal, protonephridia, and cathepsin+ cells, the latter of which consists of cryptic cell types that, until now, have only been found in planarians (Fincher et al., 2018; Figure 4A).
evidence: Figure 4A shows the UMAP projection of the combined manifolds with these cell types annotated.

claim: Cathepsin+ cells consist of cryptic cell types that, until now, have only been found in planarians.
source: The schistosome had cells mapped to the planarian stem cells, called neoblasts, as well as most of the differentiated tissues: neural, muscle, intestine, epidermis, parenchymal, protonephridia, and cathepsin+ cells, the latter of which consists of cryptic cell types that, until now, have only been found in planarians (Fincher et al., 2018; Figure 4A).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to the planarian atlas study.

claim: Mappings between schistosome and planarian cell types are supported by both known cell-type-specific marker genes and numerous homologous transcriptional regulators.
source: These mappings are supported by both known cell-type-specific marker genes and numerous homologous transcriptional regulators (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1 show the expression of these genes.

claim: The schistosome has a population of stem cells, ε-cells, that cluster with the planarian's pluripotent neoblasts, both expressing a common set of TFs (e.g. soxp2, unc4, pax6a, gcm1).
source: By mapping the schistosome stem cells to a planarian neoblast atlas (Zeng et al., 2018), we found that the schistosome has a population of stem cells, ε-cells (Wang et al., 2018), that cluster with the planarian's pluripotent neoblasts, both expressing a common set of TFs (e.g. soxp2, unc4, pax6a, gcm1) (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: Figure 4C-D shows the mapping and gene expression of these stem cell populations.

claim: The ε-cells are closely associated with juvenile development and lost in adult schistosomes.
source: The ε-cells are closely associated with juvenile development and lost in adult schistosomes (Wang et al., 2018; Nanes Sarfati et al., 2021), indicating pluripotent stem cells may be a transient population restricted to their early developmental stages.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies on schistosome stem cells.

claim: Pluripotent stem cells in schistosomes may be a transient population restricted to their early developmental stages.
source: The ε-cells are closely associated with juvenile development and lost in adult schistosomes (Wang et al., 2018; Nanes Sarfati et al., 2021), indicating pluripotent stem cells may be a transient population restricted to their early developmental stages.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ε-cell data supported by citations.

claim: Schistosomes can heal wounds but have limited regenerative ability.
source: This is consistent with the fact that, whereas schistosomes can heal wounds, they have limited regenerative ability (Wendt and Collins, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study on schistosome regeneration.

claim: SAMap linked two populations of schistosome stem cells (μ and μ') to planarian muscle progenitors, all of which express myoD.
source: SAMap also linked other schistosome stem cell populations with planarian progenitors, including two populations of schistosome stem cells – denoted as μ (Tarashansky et al., 2019) and μ' – to planarian muscle progenitors, all of which express myoD, a canonical master regulator of myogenesis (Scimone et al., 2017).
evidence: This mapping is described in the text and supported by citations.

claim: myoD is a canonical master regulator of myogenesis.
source: SAMap also linked other schistosome stem cell populations with planarian progenitors, including two populations of schistosome stem cells – denoted as μ (Tarashansky et al., 2019) and μ' – to planarian muscle progenitors, all of which express myoD, a canonical master regulator of myogenesis (Scimone et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about myoD function supported by a citation.

claim: μ and μ' cells likely represent early and late muscle progenitors, respectively.
source: These likely represent early and late muscle progenitors, respectively, as μ-cells do not yet express differentiated muscle markers such as troponin, whereas μ'-cells do (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Figure 4—figure supplement 2 shows the expression of muscle markers in these cell populations.

claim: SAMap linked 1051 cross-species pairs of cell types across all seven species.
source: In total, SAMap linked 1051 cross-species pairs of cell types, defined by the annotations used in each respective study.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the pan-species SAMap analysis.

claim: 95% of cell type pairs are supported by at least 40 enriched gene pairs.
source: Of the cell type pairs, 95% are supported by at least 40 enriched gene pairs, and 87% are supported by more than 100 gene pairs, indicating that SAMap does not spuriously connect cell types with limited overlap in transcriptional profiles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1A shows the distribution of enriched gene pairs for all mappings.

claim: 87% of cell type pairs are supported by more than 100 gene pairs.
source: Of the cell type pairs, 95% are supported by at least 40 enriched gene pairs, and 87% are supported by more than 100 gene pairs, indicating that SAMap does not spuriously connect cell types with limited overlap in transcriptional profiles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1A shows the distribution of enriched gene pairs for all mappings.

claim: SAMap does not spuriously connect cell types with limited overlap in transcriptional profiles.
source: Of the cell type pairs, 95% are supported by at least 40 enriched gene pairs, and 87% are supported by more than 100 gene pairs, indicating that SAMap does not spuriously connect cell types with limited overlap in transcriptional profiles (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the gene pair support data.

claim: The majority (81%) of cell type pairs have non-zero transitivity independent of alignment score and the number of enriched gene pairs.
source: The majority (81%) of cell type pairs have non-zero transitivity independent of alignment score and the number of enriched gene pairs (Figure 5—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplements 1–2 show the relationship between transitivity, alignment scores, and enriched gene pairs.

claim: Cell type pairs with fewer than 40 enriched gene pairs tend to have lower (<0.4) transitivity.
source: Cell type pairs with fewer than 40 enriched gene pairs tend to have lower (<0.4) transitivity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1B shows the relationship between enriched gene pairs and transitivity.

claim: 16% of mapped cell type pairs have zero edge transitivity but non-zero node transitivity.
source: 16% of mapped cell type pairs have zero edge transitivity but non-zero node transitivity. These cell types are connected to only a single member of an interconnected cell type group (motifs 2 and 3 in Figure 5B).
evidence: Figure 5B shows the motifs representing different connectivity patterns.

claim: Cell type pairs with zero edge transitivity but non-zero node transitivity may be of lower confidence and are excluded from downstream analysis.
source: Such links may be of lower confidence as they should connect to other members of the group and are thus excluded from downstream analysis.
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on the transitivity analysis.

claim: Highly connected cell type families include neural cells and contractile cells.
source: Among the interconnected groups of cell types, we identified families of neural cells and contractile cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: Figure 5C shows network graphs of highly connected cell type families.

claim: Both neural and contractile cell type families are highly transitive compared to the overall graph transitivity.
source: Both cell type families are highly transitive compared to the overall graph transitivity (bootstrap p-value<1×10−5), meaning that their constituent cell types have more transitive edges within the group than outside the group (Figure 5D).
evidence: Figure 5D shows the boxplot of node transitivities for highly connected cell type groups with statistical comparison.

claim: The dense, many-to-many connections within the contractile and neural families are each supported by at least 40 enriched gene pairs.
source: In addition, the dense, many-to-many connections within the contractile and neural families are each supported by at least 40 enriched gene pairs (Figure 5E).
evidence: Figure 5E shows the boxplot of the number of enriched gene pairs in highly connected cell type groups.

claim: The neural family includes vertebrate brain tissues, both bilaterian and cnidarian neurons, cnidarian nematocytes, and Spongilla choanocytes and apopylar cells.
source: Consistent with the nerve net hypothesis suggesting a unified origin of neural cell types (Tosches and Arendt, 2013), the neural family includes vertebrate brain tissues, both bilaterian and cnidarian neurons, cnidarian nematocytes that share the excitatory characteristics of neurons (Weir et al., 2020), and Spongilla choanocytes and apopylar cells, both of which are not considered as neurons but have been shown to express postsynaptic-like scaffolding machinery (Musser et al., 2019; Wong et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the composition of the neural cell family with supporting citations.

claim: Cnidarian nematocytes share the excitatory characteristics of neurons.
source: Consistent with the nerve net hypothesis suggesting a unified origin of neural cell types (Tosches and Arendt, 2013), the neural family includes vertebrate brain tissues, both bilaterian and cnidarian neurons, cnidarian nematocytes that share the excitatory characteristics of neurons (Weir et al., 2020), and Spongilla choanocytes and apopylar cells, both of which are not considered as neurons but have been shown to express postsynaptic-like scaffolding machinery (Musser et al., 2019; Wong et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Spongilla choanocytes and apopylar cells are not considered as neurons but have been shown to express postsynaptic-like scaffolding machinery.
source: Consistent with the nerve net hypothesis suggesting a unified origin of neural cell types (Tosches and Arendt, 2013), the neural family includes vertebrate brain tissues, both bilaterian and cnidarian neurons, cnidarian nematocytes that share the excitatory characteristics of neurons (Weir et al., 2020), and Spongilla choanocytes and apopylar cells, both of which are not considered as neurons but have been shown to express postsynaptic-like scaffolding machinery (Musser et al., 2019; Wong et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The contractile family includes myocytes in bilaterian animals, Hydra myoepithelial cells, and sponge pinacocytes and myopeptidocytes.
source: The contractile family includes myocytes in bilaterian animals, Hydra myoepithelial cells that are known to have contractile myofibrils (Buzgariu et al., 2015), and sponge pinacocytes and myopeptidocytes, both of which have been implicated to play roles in contractility (Musser et al., 2019; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the composition of the contractile cell family with supporting citations.

claim: Hydra myoepithelial cells are known to have contractile myofibrils.
source: The contractile family includes myocytes in bilaterian animals, Hydra myoepithelial cells that are known to have contractile myofibrils (Buzgariu et al., 2015), and sponge pinacocytes and myopeptidocytes, both of which have been implicated to play roles in contractility (Musser et al., 2019; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Sponge pinacocytes and myopeptidocytes have been implicated to play roles in contractility.
source: The contractile family includes myocytes in bilaterian animals, Hydra myoepithelial cells that are known to have contractile myofibrils (Buzgariu et al., 2015), and sponge pinacocytes and myopeptidocytes, both of which have been implicated to play roles in contractility (Musser et al., 2019; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A fully interconnected group contains invertebrate multipotent stem cells, including planarian and schistosome neoblasts, Hydra interstitial cells, and sponge archeocytes.
source: In contrast to the families encompassing all seven species, we also found a fully interconnected group that contains invertebrate multipotent stem cells, including planarian and schistosome neoblasts, Hydra interstitial cells, and sponge archeocytes (Alié et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the composition of the stem cell family with a supporting citation.

claim: The lack of one-to-one connections across phyla is in keeping with recent hypotheses that ancestral cell types diversified into families of cell types after speciation events.
source: The lack of one-to-one connections across phyla is in keeping with recent hypotheses that ancestral cell types diversified into families of cell types after speciation events (Arendt et al., 2016; Arendt et al., 2019).
evidence: This interpretation is supported by citations to theoretical frameworks on cell type evolution.

claim: Cell type families diversified early in animal evolution.
source: Our findings thus suggest that these cell type families diversified early in animal evolution.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cross-phyla cell type family data.

claim: SAMap identified broad transcriptomic similarity between bilaterian and non-bilaterian contractile cells that extends beyond the core contractile apparatus.
source: The high interconnectedness between cell types across broad taxonomic scales suggests that they should share ancestral transcriptional programs (Arendt et al., 2016). SAMap identified broad transcriptomic similarity between bilaterian and non-bilaterian contractile cells that extends beyond the core contractile apparatus.
evidence: This is supported by the gene enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: SAMap links a total of 23601 gene pairs, connecting 5471 unique genes, which are enriched in at least one contractile cell type pair.
source: It links a total of 23601 gene pairs, connecting 5471 unique genes, which are enriched in at least one contractile cell type pair.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the contractile cell gene analysis.

claim: Cytoskeleton and signal transduction functions are enriched in genes shared by contractile cells based on KOG functional classifications.
source: Performing functional enrichment analysis on these genes, we found cytoskeleton and signal transduction functions to be enriched (p-value<10−3) based on the KOG functional classifications (Tatusov et al., 2003) assigned by eggNOG (Figure 6A).
evidence: Figure 6A shows the enrichment of KOG functional annotations for contractile cell genes.

claim: Genes shared by contractile cells include orthology groups spanning diverse functional roles including members of the adhesion complex, actomyosin networks, and signaling pathways.
source: These genes include orthology groups spanning diverse functional roles in contractile cells, including members of the adhesion complex that connects cells, actomyosin networks that drive contractility, and signaling pathways that stimulate contraction (Figure 6B and Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Figure 6B shows the expression and enrichment of conserved muscle genes.

claim: Contractile cells near the beginning of animal evolution already possessed the broad assemblage of gene modules associated with different functional aspects of derived muscle cell types in extant animals.
source: This observation suggests that contractile cells near the beginning of animal evolution already possessed the broad assemblage of gene modules associated with different functional aspects of derived muscle cell types in extant animals.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the contractile cell gene enrichment data.

claim: Previously known core regulators involved in myocyte specification (e.g. myod and tcf4/E12) were enriched only in bilaterian or vertebrate contractile cells.
source: Previously known core regulators involved in myocyte specification (Brunet et al., 2016) were enriched only in bilaterian (e.g. myod and tcf4/E12) or vertebrate contractile cells (e.g. mef2).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B and supported by a citation.

claim: Homologs of Muscle Lim Protein (Csrp) and Forkhead Box Group 1 are enriched in contractile cells from all seven species.
source: In contrast, we found homologs of Muscle Lim Protein (Csrp) and Forkhead Box Group 1 (Larroux et al., 2008) enriched in contractile cells from all seven species.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1, and supported by a citation.

claim: FoxC is known to regulate cardiac muscle identity in vertebrates and is contractile-specific in all species except schistosome and Spongilla.
source: The Fox proteins included FoxC, which is known to regulate cardiac muscle identity in vertebrates (Brunet et al., 2016) and is contractile-specific in all species except schistosome and Spongilla.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 6B and supported by a citation.

claim: FoxG orthologs were identified to be enriched in three of the four invertebrates, suggesting that FoxG may play an underappreciated role in contractile cell specification outside vertebrates.
source: Notably, we also identified FoxG orthologs to be enriched in three of the four invertebrates (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), suggesting that FoxG may play an underappreciated role in contractile cell specification outside vertebrates.
evidence: Figure 6—figure supplement 1 shows the Fox gene family tree with enriched genes highlighted.

claim: For the family of invertebrate multipotent stem cells, 3343 genes are enriched in at least one cell type pair.
source: For the family of invertebrate multipotent stem cells, we identified 3343 genes that are enriched in at least one cell type pair and observed significant enrichment (p-value<10−3) of genes involved in translational regulation such as RNA processing, translation, and post-translational modification (Figure 6C).
evidence: Figure 6C shows the enrichment of KOG functional annotations for stem cell genes.

claim: Genes involved in translational regulation such as RNA processing, translation, and post-translational modification are significantly enriched in invertebrate multipotent stem cells.
source: For the family of invertebrate multipotent stem cells, we identified 3343 genes that are enriched in at least one cell type pair and observed significant enrichment (p-value<10−3) of genes involved in translational regulation such as RNA processing, translation, and post-translational modification (Figure 6C).
evidence: Figure 6C shows the enrichment of KOG functional annotations for stem cell genes.

claim: Cell cycle and DNA replication genes were observed in stem cells, as expected for actively dividing cells, though these were not the most enriched categories.
source: We also observed cell cycle and DNA replication genes, as expected for actively dividing cells, though these were not the most enriched categories.
evidence: This is an observation from the stem cell gene enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Shared stem cell genes comprise 979 orthology groups, 17% of which are enriched in all cell types of the stem cell family.
source: Shared stem cell genes comprise 979 orthology groups, 17% of which are enriched in all cell types of this family (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the stem cell gene analysis.

claim: Genes enriched in all stem cell types have consistently higher expression in multipotent stem cells compared to lineage-restricted stem cells and differentiated cells for all four species.
source: Importantly, these genes have consistently higher expression in the multipotent stem cells (MSCs) compared to lineage-restricted stem cells (LSCs) and differentiated cells (DCs) for all four species (Figure 6D), and may represent a large, deeply conserved gene module specifically associated with multipotency.
evidence: Figure 6D shows the boxplot of mean standardized expressions of stem cell-enriched genes in different cell types.

claim: Genes enriched in all stem cell types may represent a large, deeply conserved gene module specifically associated with multipotency.
source: Importantly, these genes have consistently higher expression in the multipotent stem cells (MSCs) compared to lineage-restricted stem cells (LSCs) and differentiated cells (DCs) for all four species (Figure 6D), and may represent a large, deeply conserved gene module specifically associated with multipotency.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the stem cell gene expression data.

claim: Transcriptional regulators enriched in MSCs across all four invertebrates include TFs from sox and klf orthology groups, the transcriptional coactivator sub1, and several chromatin modifiers including ssrp1 and kat7.
source: This included TFs from sox and klf orthology groups, the transcriptional coactivator sub1, and several chromatin modifiers, including ssrp1, a subunit of the FACT complex, and kat7, a histone acetyltransferase (Figure 6D and Supplementary file 6).
evidence: Figure 6D shows the expression of selected transcriptional regulators in stem cells.

claim: sox and klf are well-known pluripotency factors.
source: sox and klf are well-known pluripotency factors (Bialkowska et al., 2017; Sarkar and Hochedlinger, 2013), whereas the others have been studied in various processes associated with stem cell functions (MacPherson et al., 2020; Sikder et al., 2019; Zeng et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ssrp1, sub1, and kat7 have been studied in various processes associated with stem cell functions.
source: sox and klf are well-known pluripotency factors (Bialkowska et al., 2017; Sarkar and Hochedlinger, 2013), whereas the others have been studied in various processes associated with stem cell functions (MacPherson et al., 2020; Sikder et al., 2019; Zeng et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The conserved enrichment of sox, klf, sub1, ssrp1, and kat7 in invertebrate MSCs suggests that their functional role in stem cells may be more phylogenetically ancient than previously appreciated.
source: The conserved enrichment of these transcriptional regulators in invertebrate MSCs suggests that their functional role in stem cells may be more phylogenetically ancient than previously appreciated.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the conserved stem cell transcriptional regulator data.

claim: Cell types evolve as their gene expression programs change either as integrated units or via evolutionary splitting that results in separate derived programs.
source: Cell types evolve as their gene expression programs change either as integrated units or via evolutionary splitting that results in separate derived programs.
evidence: This is presented as an established concept in cell type evolution.

claim: SAMap aligns cell atlases in two mutually reinforcing directions, mapping both the genes and the cells, with each feeding back into the other.
source: Here, we map single-cell atlases between evolutionarily distant species in a manner that accounts for the complexity of gene evolution. SAMap aligns cell atlases in two mutually reinforcing directions, mapping both the genes and the cells, with each feeding back into the other.
evidence: This describes the core algorithmic approach of SAMap.

claim: SAMap scales well to the majority of presently available whole-organism cell atlases.
source: Although this algorithm scales well to the majority of presently available whole-organism cell atlases, the size of single-cell datasets will continue to increase.
evidence: This is supported by the runtime and memory usage data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The most memory-intensive steps in SAMap are the neighborhood coarsening of cross-species edges and the cross-species imputation of gene expression to calculate gene-gene correlations.
source: The most memory-intensive steps in SAMap are the neighborhood coarsening of cross-species edges and the cross-species imputation of gene expression to calculate gene-gene correlations, both of which could be intractable for datasets containing millions of cells.
evidence: This is a technical description of SAMap's computational limitations.

claim: SAMap allows identification of one-to-one cell type concordance between animals in the same phylum.
source: SAMap allows us to identify one-to-one cell type concordance between animals in the same phylum, whereas between phyla, we observe interconnected cell types forming distinct families.
evidence: This is a summary of the mapping results across different taxonomic scales.

claim: Between phyla, SAMap observes interconnected cell types forming distinct families.
source: SAMap allows us to identify one-to-one cell type concordance between animals in the same phylum, whereas between phyla, we observe interconnected cell types forming distinct families.
evidence: This is a summary of the mapping results across different taxonomic scales shown in Figure 5C.

claim: These findings support the notion that cell types evolve via hierarchical diversification.
source: These findings support the notion that cell types evolve via hierarchical diversification (Arendt et al., 2019), resulting in cell type families composed of evolutionarily related cell types sharing a regulatory gene expression program that originated in their common ancestor.
evidence: This interpretation is supported by a citation to a theoretical framework on cell type evolution.

claim: Cell type families are composed of evolutionarily related cell types sharing a regulatory gene expression program that originated in their common ancestor.
source: These findings support the notion that cell types evolve via hierarchical diversification (Arendt et al., 2019), resulting in cell type families composed of evolutionarily related cell types sharing a regulatory gene expression program that originated in their common ancestor.
evidence: This is part of the interpretation of the cell type family data.

claim: One-to-one cell type homologies should exist only if no further cell type diversification has occurred since the speciation.
source: One-to-one cell type homologies should exist only if no further cell type diversification has occurred since the speciation.
evidence: This is a theoretical statement about when one-to-one homologies are expected.

claim: Many of the aligned cell types identified by SAMap share expression of transcription factors known to play important roles in cell type differentiation.
source: Notably, many of the aligned cell types we identified share expression of transcription factors known to play important roles in cell type differentiation, suggesting SAMap alignments based on mutual connectivity reflect evolutionary homology, rather than convergent functional similarity.
evidence: This is supported by the transcription factor expression data shown in Figures 4B, 6B, and 6D.

claim: SAMap alignments based on mutual connectivity reflect evolutionary homology, rather than convergent functional similarity.
source: Notably, many of the aligned cell types we identified share expression of transcription factors known to play important roles in cell type differentiation, suggesting SAMap alignments based on mutual connectivity reflect evolutionary homology, rather than convergent functional similarity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the shared transcription factor expression in mapped cell types.

claim: SAMap provides a roadmap for tracing cell type evolutionary history and identifying the molecular changes in transcription factor regulatory complexes that have driven cell type diversification.
source: SAMap thus provides a roadmap for tracing cell type evolutionary history and identifying the molecular changes in transcription factor regulatory complexes that have driven cell type diversification.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the potential applications of SAMap.

claim: Paralog substitution can occur due to differential loss or retention of cell-type-specific expression patterns of genes that were duplicated in the common ancestor.
source: Paralog substitution can occur due to differential loss or retention of cell-type-specific expression patterns of genes that were duplicated in the common ancestor (Shafer et al., 2020; Studer and Robinson-Rechavi, 2009) or due to compensating upregulation of paralogs following a loss-of-function mutation acquired by an ortholog (El-Brolosy et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies on paralog evolution.

claim: Paralog substitution can occur due to compensating upregulation of paralogs following a loss-of-function mutation acquired by an ortholog.
source: Paralog substitution can occur due to differential loss or retention of cell-type-specific expression patterns of genes that were duplicated in the common ancestor (Shafer et al., 2020; Studer and Robinson-Rechavi, 2009) or due to compensating upregulation of paralogs following a loss-of-function mutation acquired by an ortholog (El-Brolosy et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study on genetic compensation.

claim: Considering the observation that paralog substitutions occur at higher rates for more recent paralogs, the genetic compensation scenario is expected to be more likely, at least between frog and zebrafish.
source: Considering our observation that paralog substitutions occur at higher rates for more recent paralogs, which should be more capable of functionally compensating for each other, we expect the latter scenario to be more likely, at least between frog and zebrafish.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the paralog age-dependent substitution rate data.

claim: Paralog substitutions may play an important role in cell type diversification, enabling newly evolved sister cell types to subfunctionalize via the use of distinct paralogs.
source: Paralog substitutions may also play an important role in cell type diversification, enabling newly evolved sister cell types to subfunctionalize via the use of distinct paralogs.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential role of paralog substitutions in evolution.

claim: SAMap can catalyze the annotation of new cell atlases from non-model organisms.
source: Besides applications in evolutionary biology, we anticipate SAMap can catalyze the annotation of new cell atlases from non-model organisms, which often represents a substantial bottleneck requiring extensive manual curation and prior knowledge.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential applications of SAMap.

claim: SAMap's ability to use existing atlases to inform the annotation of cell types in related species will keep improving as more datasets become available.
source: Its ability to use the existing atlases to inform the annotation of cell types in related species will keep improving as more datasets become available to better sample the diversity of cell types throughout the animal kingdom.
evidence: This is a prediction about the future performance of SAMap.
